_comment: Canonical terminology. Across 1146 items written in hundreds of separate sessions, nothing else keeps the same thing called the same name. 'avoid' lists real synonyms a competent writer would otherwise reach for; the validator rejects them and names the replacement. To use a variant deliberately — usually to tell the reader that other people say it — add allowVariants: [word] to that item's frontmatter. That makes it a visible decision instead of drift.

canonical.definition: The outer protective covering fitted over insulation.
The material that slows heat transfer. Never 'lagging', which is ambiguous between the material and the whole trade.
The lambda value of a material, in W/(m·K). Spell it out; do not assume the reader knows the symbol.
Resistance to heat flow. Do not call it R-value; that convention carries assumptions about units and thickness that vary by country.
The layer preventing water vapour reaching a cold surface. American spelling throughout the project, matching the existing chapter 16 title.
Preventing condensation forming on cold surfaces. Named in the employer's own scope, so it gets one consistent English name.
Insulation to retain heat in a system hotter than its surroundings.
Insulation on a system colder than its surroundings.
Preformed cylindrical insulation that fits a pipe.
Flexible roll or mat insulation, as used on ductwork and large surfaces.
Metal strap fastened around insulation or jacketing.
Work where a fall could cause injury. Singular 'height', matching regulatory usage.
A platform to stand and work on, as required by regulation above stated heights.

canonical.definition: The document stating how a specific job is to be carried out on a specific site.
The person directing the crew on site. Use consistently; readers need one word for the person they ask.
